cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what remains after the change is being held.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Pick someone you have been carrying more of lately. Offer them something small and true, and take what they offer back, without waving it off. No deadline on it.
cells.core:
You came through something that took things apart, and you are standing in what is left of it. You keep it steady with form — a routine, a room put back the way it works, a promise you show up to. That is not stalling. What the clearing left gets held before it is handed to anyone.

The exchange around you is running on one side. You have been steadying people and taking nothing back from them. So choose one of them and open it the other way once: your offer, their offer, neither one cancelled out. The rest of what you carry can keep tipping one way for a while — leave it. Try the balance on one thin thread before you call the whole account fair.
cells.sheetLine: Hold what's left. But let one exchange go both ways.
cells.verb: holding what the change left standing, keeping it steady while it settles
cells.place: the clearing after the ending, where what remains has to be held or it scatters

cells.tense: You are already bracing for the next change, holding this one against the door.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Set the grip down once. Walk toward the next thing that tugs at you, with no plan and no verdict waiting at the end.
cells.core:
You are guarding what the ending left you. More than guarding — bracing for the next round before it gets here, tightening every form so nothing can come in and take this again. It reads as devotion to what you won. It closes the doors your clearing opened.

Something is already tugging at you. A room you keep thinking about, a person you keep almost calling. Go toward one of those before you have decided it is safe or sensible. No plan, no commitment, no verdict. What you get close to is smaller than the dread was.

Let yourself be pulled a little way toward what you might feel. That is where the next thing lives. If this is wrong, it cost you a walk and showed you what the pull is made of.
cells.sheetLine: Stop guarding it. Follow the thing that's already tugging.
cells.verb: holding what the change left standing, keeping it steady while it settles
cells.place: the clearing after the ending, where what remains has to be held or it scatters

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed, keeping the shape of what was.
cells.act: refuse the pull off course, once more
cells.ask: Take one direction you already picked after the ending, and when something small pulls at it, hold where you are. Just once. No further plan needed.
cells.core:
Something ended and you kept holding on at the edge of it. The forms around you are the ones from before — the routine, the usual seat, the version of yourself that belonged to what is finished. You carry the key to a shut door.

You made at least one choice after it, though. You can find it if you look. That heading — a habit, a no, a place you decided to keep going — is still yours. When something small pulls against it, do not follow the pull one time. Refuse it once and stay where you stand.

Direction comes from feeling something, and you know which heading you meant. Hold it once, and the room starts to move.
cells.sheetLine: The door already shut. You're still holding its key.
cells.verb: holding what the change left standing, keeping it steady while it settles
cells.place: the clearing after the ending, where what remains has to be held or it scatters

cells.tense: You are deciding what stays and moving it into place, and calling that just how things are.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Settle one thing still waiting since the clearing — a message, a box, a bill — the day you decide it, and tell nobody you did.
cells.core:
Since the ending you have been sorting. What stays, what goes, where it gets put and who it gets kept for. The calls were made and the room is in order, and if someone asked you would say it sorted itself out.

It did not. Your hand is on every arrangement, and nobody is saying so. Take something still waiting on you — a message, a box, a bill — and settle it the day you decide, without announcing it to anyone first. The order around you is work, and you are the one who did it. Let one act stand as yours, without filing it under how things happened to go.

The order is yours. It does not need a speech to hold.
cells.sheetLine: The order isn't luck. You did that. Say so.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this person has actually cleared and completed something — Preservation as a transic says only that something produced by change needs holding before it is shared, not that they finished a clearing. A reader could reasonably say nothing has ended yet, they are just tired or stuck. The ask is one visible act with a person, so it still teaches them something about exchange even if my read of their situation is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the push is fair, and the fairness is what makes it fast' in the exemplar — it flatters momentum; I have written toward plainness instead.
